name: villalona hair salon
website: https://www.vagaro.com/villalonahairsalon (booking page); the domain villalonahairsalon.com is a parked 'for sale' page
what_they_do: Hair salon on Georges Road with a team of stylists serving appointments and walk-ins, Mon-Sat. Its only web presence is a Vagaro booking page, which is also what Google uses for its 'Book online' button; services and prices are managed inside Vagaro rather than on a site of its own.
customers: Neighbourhood clients in North Brunswick, long-tenure regulars and walk-ins; Saturday opens at 8am.

size_signals.signal: A reviewer describes a 'large' team, quality products and the business growing 'to multiple locations', naming the owner as Rachel
4.6 from 84 Google reviews; Mon-Fri 9-6, Sat 8-5; books through Vagaro

website_review.primary_cta: Book online via Vagaro (from the Google listing)
website_review.online_booking_or_quote: Vagaro - real online booking that Google's listing links to
website_review.trust_signals: 84 Google reviews at 4.6; Vagaro profile carries services and staff calendars (not readable by me - bot wall)
website_review.out_of_date_signs: the brand domain villalonahairsalon.com now serves a parked 'this domain may be for sale' page with no salon content
website_review.search_basics: no site to carry titles, descriptions, service pages or schema; brand searches land on a domain broker or third-party directories
top_issues: No website: brand searches hit a parked domain, so the salon's own name does not lead to a page about it
Services, prices and hours exist only inside Vagaro or on directories, so a crawler or agent has little to quote from the salon's own words
No contact form or click-to-call page; the only routes are Vagaro or the phone

agent_readiness.notes: Findable 2: GBP has hours, phone and booking link. Answerable 1: hours are public but service and price text lives only inside Vagaro, and there is no schema or owned copy. Bookable 2: Vagaro is a platform Google's booking features integrate with and the map listing exposes it; however the Vagaro page returned an Incapsula bot-check to me, so I could not confirm the service menu or absence of a captcha.

operations_signals.signal: Appointments are booked through Vagaro, so the schedule is already digital and appointment reminders/no-show handling can be automated on top of it
Former domain is parked with a for-sale notice - brand traffic leaks to a broker instead of the salon

top_opportunities.opportunity: Put a real site on the brand domain (or recover it) with the service menu, prices, stylist bios and an embedded Vagaro booking widget
top_opportunities.evidence: villalonahairsalon.com is a parked domain-for-sale page; booking lives only on Vagaro

top_opportunities.opportunity: Publish service menu and price ranges as text plus Salon JSON-LD so agents can answer 'how much is a colour?' without opening a booking widget
top_opportunities.evidence: No readable price or service text on any salon-owned page

top_opportunities.opportunity: Add missed-call text-back and automated reminders around the Vagaro calendar to cut no-shows
top_opportunities.evidence: Digital calendar already in place via Vagaro; phone remains the only fallback channel

scores.reasons: Gap 3 - booking is genuinely solved via Vagaro; what is missing is an owned site and readable service/price content. Ability to pay 3 - multi-location growth described in reviews and 84 reviews at 4.6. Ease 4 - a site plus schema, no platform migration. Evidence 4 - GBP, parked domain and Vagaro link verified, but Vagaro's content was behind a bot wall.
